lessons.title: Sentences I
lines: the quick fox runs by the barn while birds sing softly at dawn. we planted seeds in our garden and watched the green leaves grow. a gentle breeze moved across the bright field. typing a full sentence takes patience attention and practice. practice each day at school. careful practice helps each learner type with calm focus. practice each day at school.

lessons.title: Shift Keys: Capitals
lines: My name is Sam. The sun is bright today, and we live in Karachi. Every new sentence begins with a capital letter. Use the opposite Shift hand, keep your eyes on the text, and type slowly. Good habits grow when we practise with care. Keep typing with care. Type each capital with care. Read each sentence first. Keep each space clear.

lessons.title: Commas and Periods
lines: I like apples, pears, and plums. First we run, then we jump. She reads, writes, and draws. A comma gives a sentence a small pause, while a period brings it to a stop. Type each mark carefully and keep the spaces in place. Type with calm care. Read each sentence before you move on. Check each mark. Type each comma with care.

lessons.title: Full Sentences
lines: The Bridge School has bright, curious students. We practise typing every single day, because good habits build strong, lasting skills. Each careful sentence improves accuracy, rhythm, and confidence. Look at the next word, use the right finger, and let your hands learn the path. Practise each sentence with patience. Read ahead and keep the rhythm steady.

lessons.title: Question Practice
lines: Where did you put my book? Why is the sky so blue today? Who wants to play outside? Questions begin with curiosity and end with a question mark. Read each question in your mind, then type it with care. Keep the spaces, capitals, and punctuation accurate. Read each question before you begin. Type with care. Check each space and mark.

lessons.title: Speed Drill I
lines: Practice makes progress, not perfection. Every keystroke builds a stronger habit, and every accurate sentence helps your hands move with confidence. Focus on your words, not the keys. Keep a steady rhythm, breathe normally, and let your fingers remember what they have learned. Read the next sentence before you type it. Let accuracy lead the way, and allow speed to grow from calm practice.

lessons.title: Speed Drill II
lines: Reading and typing go hand in hand. Look a few words ahead, keep your hands in position, and allow the next letter to arrive naturally. Small daily practice adds up quickly. When a mistake appears, stay calm, correct it when the mode allows, and continue the paragraph. Keep your eyes moving forward, use both hands evenly, and let each careful sentence become smoother.

lessons.title: Paragraph Challenge
lines: Learning to type well takes patience and practice. Each lesson adds a new skill to your fingers, but real fluency grows when you connect those skills in complete thoughts. Read the paragraph first, notice its rhythm, and then type without looking down. Accuracy gives speed a strong foundation, while calm attention helps every sentence become smoother. Read ahead, keep your shoulders relaxed, and trust the fingers that have practised each row.

lessons.title: Final Challenge
lines: Congratulations on reaching the final lesson. You have worked hard to build this skill, from finding the home row to typing complete paragraphs with capitals and punctuation. Keep practising, trust the correct fingers, and remember that accuracy comes first. With steady effort, your hands will grow faster, calmer, and more confident every day. Continue to practise a little each day, read ahead, and stay relaxed when a sentence feels challenging. Your careful work has built a skill you can use in every school subject and every new idea you write.
